title: The Main Themes of the Quran
subtitle: Start here: fifteen themes, from the oneness of God to fighting and peace, each in its own words, with the study that follows it through the whole book
summary: The Quran is not arranged by subject. Apart from the short opening prayer, its 114 surahs run roughly from longest to shortest, and most of them move between several themes at once. Read straight through, it can feel like a collection of sermons, arguments, stories, laws and prayers, and it is. But a small number of themes return on nearly every page, and together they are what the Quran teaches. God is one, with no partner and no son. He made the world, and it is full of signs pointing to Him. He sent prophets to every people with that one message, the last of them Muhammad, and sent down the Quran through him in Arabic. Every person will be raised and judged on the Last Day and go to the Garden or the Fire, by their faith and their deeds. So believe, pray, give, fast and make the pilgrimage; keep the law; and know who is a believer, who is not, and who only pretends. Around these stand the Quran's words about Jews and Christians, about Jesus and Mary, about war and peace, and about the unseen world of angels and jinn. This study gives each theme a few passages in the Quran's own words; the other studies on this site take each one through the whole book. The views show where each theme falls: the early Meccan surahs are full of God, creation and the Day; the law, the fighting and the People of the Book belong to Medina.

views.title: Fifteen themes
views.note: In roughly the order of importance the Quran itself gives them.

groups.title: God is one
groups.note: The first and greatest theme: there is no god but God, and nothing is like Him. Full study: God in the Quran.

refs.label: “He is God, the One … He begets not, nor was He begotten”
The Throne Verse
refs.note: “God! There is no god except He, the Living, the Everlasting.”

refs.label: “His are the Most Beautiful Names”
“God does not forgive association with Him”
“He has inscribed for Himself mercy”

groups.title: Creation and its signs
groups.note: The world is full of signs of its Maker, and of the resurrection. Full study: Signs in Creation.

refs.label: “Signs for people who understand”
“And of His signs …”
“A sign for them in the dead land: We give it life”

groups.title: The prophets
groups.note: One message to every people, and the punishment of those who refused. Full study: The Prophets and Their Stories.

refs.label: “To every community We sent a messenger”
“There is no god but I, so worship Me”
“As We had inspired Noah and the prophets after him”
“To strengthen your heart”

groups.title: Muhammad
groups.note: A man and a messenger, the last of the prophets, to be followed and obeyed. Full study: Muhammad in the Quran.

refs.label: “The Messenger of God, and the seal of the prophets”
“I am only a human being like you”
“We did not send you except as mercy to mankind”
“Whoever obeys the Messenger is obeying God”

groups.title: The Quran
groups.note: God's own speech in Arabic, beyond imitation. Full study: The Quran About Itself.

refs.label: “An Arabic Quran, so that you may understand”
“Produce a chapter like these”
“We never nullify a verse … unless We bring one better”
“We will surely preserve it”

groups.title: The Last Day
groups.note: The end of the world, the resurrection, the judgment, the Garden and the Fire. Full study: The Last Day, Paradise and Hell.

refs.label: “When the sun is rolled up”
“Whoever has done an atom's weight of good will see it”
The scales, heavy and light
Rivers of water, milk, wine and honey
“Every time their skins are cooked, We will replace them”

groups.title: Faith, deeds and forgiveness
groups.note: Those who believe and do good works are saved; God forgives those who repent; no one carries another's sins. Full study: Sin, Repentance and Salvation.

refs.label: “Except those who believe, and do good works”
“Do not despair of God's mercy”
“No soul bears the burdens of another soul”
“I do not know what will be done with me, or with you”

groups.title: Worship
groups.note: Prayer, alms, the fast and the pilgrimage, and the constant remembrance of God. Full study: Worship.

refs.label: The Opening
The fast of Ramadan
The pilgrimage, “a duty to God”
Who the alms are for
“Righteousness does not consist of turning your faces towards the East and the West”

groups.title: The law
groups.note: Commandments much like Moses', rules for food, killing, theft and money, and justice even to enemies. Full study: The Law.

refs.label: “Some of the wisdom your Lord has revealed to you”
Forbidden foods, and “Today I have perfected your religion”
“As for the thief … cut their hands”
“God has permitted commerce, and has forbidden usury”
“Let not the hatred of a certain people prevent you from acting justly”

groups.title: Women and the family
groups.note: One soul, equal reward, and a family law that treats men and women differently. Full study: Women, Marriage and Family.

refs.label: “Created you from a single soul”
“Muslim men and Muslim women …”
“Two, or three, or four”
“Men are the protectors and maintainers of women”
“The male receives the equivalent of the share of two females”

groups.title: Believers, unbelievers and hypocrites
groups.note: The three kinds of people, and how believers live among the others. Full study: Believers, Unbelievers and Hypocrites.

refs.label: “Successful are the believers”
“God bears witness that the hypocrites are liars”
“There shall be no compulsion in religion”
“Believers are not to take disbelievers for friends instead of believers”

groups.title: Jews and Christians
groups.note: Praised, blamed, argued with and invited. Full study: Jews and Christians: the People of the Book.

refs.label: “Come to terms common between us and you”
“They are not alike”
“Those who write the Scripture with their own hands”
“Do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies”

groups.title: Jesus and Mary
groups.note: Born of a virgin, a prophet of miracles; not God's son, and not crucified. Full study: Jesus and Mary in the Quran.

refs.label: The annunciation
Birds of clay, the blind, the leper, the dead
“They did not kill him, nor did they crucify him”
“Do not say, ‘Three’”

groups.title: Fighting and peace
groups.note: Patience at Mecca; at Medina fighting permitted, then commanded, with limits. Full study: Fighting and Peace.

refs.label: “Repel evil with good”
“Permission is given to those who are fought against”
“Fight … those who fight you, but do not commit aggression”
“If they incline towards peace, then incline towards it”
“Kill the polytheists wherever you find them”
“Until they pay the due tax”

groups.title: Angels, jinn and Satan
groups.note: The unseen world: God's servants, a second race of fire, and the enemy. Full study: Angels, Jinn and Satan.

refs.label: Satan will not bow to Adam
The two recorders
“We have heard a wondrous Quran”
“From the evil of the sneaky whisperer”

views.title: Nöldeke's periods
views.note: The same passages in the four periods of Theodor Nöldeke's dating of the surahs: God, creation and the Day fill the early Meccan surahs; the law, the People of the Book and the fighting come at Medina.
